meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: pointing at something a little way off
Вон отсюда! = get out of here!. Core Russian part meaning 'over there' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: It is a question of upbringing, after all.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.

examples.text: Всю морковку почистили, ещё дудку сделали. Молодец.

who makes a flute out of a carrot.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'potatoes' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я целый год ела только картошку.
examples.trans: I ate only potatoes for a whole year.

examples.text: Ты останешься на кухне чистить картошку.
examples.trans: You will stay in the kitchen peeling potatoes.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.
For grain, herbs, potatoes, etc. Common masculine noun meaning 'sack, bag' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned.
They bought a whole sack of potatoes.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'Mikhailovich', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Что за бред? Герман Михайлович просто попросил кофе.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? German Mikhailovich simply asked for coffee.
German Mikhailovich, Nagiyev has arrived out there.

meanings.note: praise, said to a man, woman or child
Old-fashioned. Common masculine noun meaning 'well done; good person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

meanings.note: colloquial for морковь; also figuratively an enticing reward

examples.text: И в конце нас всех ждёт вкусная морковка!
examples.trans: And at the end a tasty carrot is waiting for us all!
There is fresh carrot in the soup.

examples.text: У нас есть взрослая цель — морковка.
examples.trans: We have a grown-up goal: the carrot.

examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

потерпеть.gloss: to be patient for a while, to endure

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
meanings.note: Often imperative: потерпи!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпеть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be patient for a while, to endure', paired with 'терпеть'.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.
Hang on for five more minutes.

examples.text: Послушай меня, Ваня. Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: Listen to me, Vanya. We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чистить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will peel, clean'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и почистить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will peel on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют почистить.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will peel.

meanings.note: Простите! = sorry! forgive me!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
Imperative: прости / простите. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will you keep (company)'.

examples.trans: How formal, will you keep me company?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и составить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will you keep on time.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.note: often + с + instrumental, or used absolutely

examples.text: Мы за два года тут не справимся.
examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

examples.text: Мы обязательно справимся и с этим.
examples.trans: We will definitely cope with this too.
